title: kv-cache: improve eviction/paging/spillover and scheduling heuristics to reduce fragmentation and tail latency
author: Anika Desai
description: Motivation: We see sustained tail latency and increased GPU memory fragmentation under mixed sequence-length workloads. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes across the KV cache, background paging/spillover, and the scheduler to reduce fragmentation, avoid pathological eviction churn, and improve tail P99 latency. Summary of changes: 1) New segmented eviction policy: introduces a generational LRU segmentation that separates short-lived prefix entries from long-lived context caches so evictions target the hot-evictable segment first. 2) Defragmentation pass: periodic, low-priority defragmentation that coalesces free blocks in GPU memory without blocking inference streams. 3) Spillover/paging improvements: asynchronous spill-over to host pageable memory with an adaptive prefetch window (based on observed sequence-length distribution) and backpressure signals to the scheduler. 4) Scheduler heuristics: affinity-aware routing that prefers devices with colocated KV segments, and a conservative batching fallback that avoids aggressive batch sizes when spillover is active. 5) Observability and safety: new metrics (kv.evictions.segmented, kv.spill.pages, kv.defrag.cycles), and a feature-flag gate for enabling the full coordinated behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked) - [x] Unit tests for eviction and paging logic - [x] Microbenchmarks showing tail improvements - [x] Integration tests for scheduler interplay - [x] Feature flag and config knobs Implementation notes: Changes touch low-level allocation and scheduling code; implemented careful lock-free handoff between eviction and pager threads, with a single-control atomic to avoid double-free. The defragmentation pass runs at low priority and yields to inference; preemptible checkpoints ensure no long stall. Benchmarks: End-to-end mixed workload: P99 latency reduced by ~18% and 95th token generation cost reduced by ~12% on our heavy-mix benchmark. Memory fragmentation (measured as unusable free segments ratio) improved from 28% to 6% under long-running simulated traffic. Backwards compatibility: behavior is behind a feature flag (runtime.kv.segmented_eviction = true) and defaults to off for customers on Dedicated/Private until validated. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: unexpected page-fault latency when spilling to host. Mitigation: adaptive prefetch and conservative batching when spillover is active. - Risk: increased CPU load from pager/defrag threads. Mitigation: configurable rate-limits and affinity to spare cores. Related work: follows up on ENG-1512 (defrag pilot) and ENG-1458 (kv paging prototype).
